findings.evidence: Systematic review and meta-analysis using Cochrane, CAMARADES and SYRCLE bias tools; 22 studies comprising 381 rabbits and rodents.
findings.effect_size: LVEF +9.87% (95% CI 7.25-12.50); considerable between-study heterogeneity
findings.effect_size_source_sentence: Nevertheless, due to the small number of studies and considerable heterogeneity, future translational studies must be designed to diminish between-study discrepancies and increase similarity to the clinical landscape.

findings.claim: In animal ischaemic stroke, IL-1 receptor antagonist reduced infarct volume by 36.2%, but adjusting for ~30 theoretically missing (unpublished) studies cut efficacy to 21.9%, and studies not reporting allocation concealment reported larger effects.
findings.claim_source_sentence: Overall, IL-1 RA reduced infarct volume by 36.2 % (95 % confidence interval 31.6-40.7, n = 76 comparisons from 1283 animals).
findings.evidence: Updated CAMARADES systematic review and meta-analysis of 25 data sources; assessed study quality and publication bias via trim-and-fill.
findings.effect_size: efficacy 36.2% falls to 21.9% after adjusting for ~30 missing studies
findings.effect_size_source_sentence: Assessments for publication bias suggest 30 theoretically missing studies which reduce efficacy to 21.9 % (17.3-26.4).

findings.claim: A preclinical meta-analysis of Fructus Psoraleae ingredients for osteoporosis pooled 16 small-animal studies with a mean CAMARADES quality score of only 5.25/10, calling for large, rigorous confirmatory trials.
findings.claim_source_sentence: The risk of bias score of included studies ranged from 4 to 7 with an average score of 5.25.
findings.evidence: Systematic review and meta-analysis using the modified CAMARADES 10-item quality checklist across multiple databases; 16 studies, 379 animals.
findings.effect_size: mean CAMARADES score 5.25/10 (range 4-7); 16 studies, 379 animals
findings.effect_size_source_sentence: Overall, 16 studies focusing on 379 animals were enrolled into the study.

findings.claim: A meta-analysis of exercise and seizure susceptibility could pool only 15 animal studies (543 animals), with 13 of 15 using males only and high heterogeneity limiting conclusions.
findings.claim_source_sentence: Fifteen studies were included in the final analysis (543 animals), 13 of them used male animals, and Wistar rats were the most commonly studied species used in the studies (355 animals).
findings.evidence: Systematic review and random-effects meta-analysis using SYRCLE risk-of-bias and CAMARADES checklists.
findings.effect_size: 15 studies, 543 animals; 13/15 male-only; high heterogeneity
findings.effect_size_source_sentence: The high heterogeneity in our meta-analysis is attributable to various factors, including the number of animals used in each study and the limited number of similar studies.

findings.claim: A systematic review of mitochondrial transplantation in Alzheimer's and Parkinson's animal models found only 7 of 231 identified studies met inclusion criteria, reflecting a thin, low-quality preclinical evidence base.
findings.claim_source_sentence: The initial search resulted in 231 studies, and after screening the titles and abstracts, 30 studies were recognized. Finally, 7 studies met the inclusion criteria.
findings.evidence: Systematic review using CAMARADES checklists and the SYRCLE risk-of-bias tool across PubMed, Scopus, EMBASE and Google Scholar to October 2024.
findings.effect_size: 7 of 231 identified studies met inclusion criteria
findings.effect_size_source_sentence: The initial search resulted in 231 studies, and after screening the titles and abstracts, 30 studies were recognized. Finally, 7 studies met the inclusion criteria.

findings.claim: A meta-analysis of biomaterials for ischemic stroke showed pronounced funnel-plot asymmetry; trim-and-fill estimated 19 missing studies, cutting the lesion-volume effect from -2.98 to -1.91 SMD, with median CAMARADES quality only 5.5/10.
findings.claim_source_sentence: Additionally, trim and fill analysis estimated 19 "missing" studies for the lesion volume outcome adjusting the effect size to -1.91 (95% CI: -2.44, -1.38).
findings.evidence: Systematic review and meta-analysis of 66 publications (44 studies/86 comparisons in meta-analysis) using the CAMARADES checklist and DerSimonian-Laird random effects.
findings.effect_size: lesion-volume SMD -2.98 -> -1.91 after trim-and-fill (19 missing); CAMARADES median 5.5/10
findings.effect_size_source_sentence: The median score on the CAMARADES checklist was 5.5/10 (IQR 4.25-6).

findings.claim: A meta-analysis of gene therapies for spinal cord injury reported strong locomotor benefit (SMD 2.07) but significant funnel-plot asymmetry indicating publication bias and a low median CAMARADES score of 4, with allocation concealment and sample-size calculations frequently missing.
findings.claim_source_sentence: There was significant asymmetry in the funnel plots of both outcome measures indicating the presence of publication bias.
findings.evidence: Systematic review and random-effects meta-analysis of 71 studies using a modified CAMARADES checklist; PROSPERO-registered.
findings.effect_size: locomotor SMD 2.07 (95% CI 1.68-2.47); median CAMARADES 4 (IQR 3-5)
findings.effect_size_source_sentence: We used a modified CAMARADES (Collaborative Approach to Meta-Analysis and Review of Animal Data in Experimental Studies) checklist to assess the risk of bias, finding that the median score was 4 (IQR: 3-5).
findings.study_system: animal models of spinal cord injury (gene therapy)

findings.claim: In the landmark Reproducibility Project: Psychology, only 36% of 100 replications reached statistical significance versus 97% of the original studies, and replication effect sizes averaged half the originals.
findings.claim_source_sentence: Ninety-seven percent of original studies had statistically significant results. Thirty-six percent of replications had statistically significant results; 47% of original effect sizes were in the 95% confidence interval of the replication effect size; 39% of effects were subjectively rated to have replicated the original result; and if no bias in original results is assumed, combining original and replication results left 68% with statistically significant effects.
findings.evidence: Coordinated replications of 100 experimental and correlational studies from three psychology journals using high-powered designs and original materials.
findings.effect_size: 97% original significant vs 36% replications significant; replication effects ~half of originals
findings.effect_size_source_sentence: Replication effects were half the magnitude of original effects, representing a substantial decline.

findings.claim: A prominent critique argued the Reproducibility Project: Psychology contained three statistical errors and that, properly analyzed, the data are consistent with high reproducibility, illustrating unresolved disagreement over how replication should be measured.
findings.claim_source_sentence: We show that this article contains three statistical errors and provides no support for such a conclusion.
findings.evidence: Technical comment reanalyzing the Open Science Collaboration replication data, disputing its low-reproducibility conclusion.
findings.effect_size: qualitative reversal: reanalysis argues reproducibility is 'quite high'
findings.effect_size_source_sentence: Indeed, the data are consistent with the opposite conclusion, namely, that the reproducibility of psychological science is quite high.

findings.claim: Bayesian modeling of the 36% psychology reproducibility rate implies large publication bias: in a literature dominated by positive findings, roughly 55-98 negative results were expected to have occurred before one negative result was published.
findings.claim_source_sentence: Publication bias was large, assuming a literature with 90% positive findings, indicating that negative evidence was expected to have been observed 55-98 times before one negative result was published.
findings.evidence: Applied Bayes' theorem to the Open Science Collaboration 36% reproducibility rate to estimate original power, prior probability and publication bias.
findings.effect_size: expected 55-98 unpublished negatives per published negative; original power estimated 48-75%
findings.effect_size_source_sentence: We estimate a plausible range for the prior probability of this body of research, suggesting expected statistical power in the original studies of 48-75%, producing (positive) findings that were expected to be true 41-62% of the time.
findings.study_system: psychology literature (Bayesian reanalysis of OSC replications)

findings.claim: An automated analysis of 57,909 psychology articles (2010-2021) found the median proportion of significant p-values per article stayed constant at 69% despite a decade of reform, though median sample sizes rose from 105 to 190.
findings.claim_source_sentence: Compared to articles that were published in and before 2015, the median number of reported p-values per article has decreased from 14 to 12, whereas the median proportion of significant p-values per article remained constant at 69%.
findings.evidence: Text-mining of 57,909 articles from 12 journals with JATSdecoder, tracking p-values, confidence intervals, power analysis, corrections and sample sizes over 12 years.
findings.effect_size: 69% significant p-values per article (unchanged); median sample size rose 105 -> 190
findings.effect_size_source_sentence: The overall median estimated sample size has increased from 105 to 190.

findings.claim: Published estimates of the cost of irreproducible preclinical studies range from US$28 billion per year in the USA alone to over US$200 billion per year worldwide.
findings.claim_source_sentence: Estimates of the cost of irreproducible preclinical studies range from 28 billion USD per year in the USA alone (Freedman et al. in PLoS Biol 13(6):e1002165, 2015) to over 200 billion USD per year worldwide (Chalmers and Glasziou in Lancet 374:86-89, 2009).
findings.evidence: Perspective on reproducibility spanning preclinical, psychological and computational-simulation research, compiling published irreproducibility cost estimates.
findings.effect_size: US$28B/year (US) to >US$200B/year (worldwide)
findings.effect_size_source_sentence: Estimates of the cost of irreproducible preclinical studies range from 28 billion USD per year in the USA alone (Freedman et al. in PLoS Biol 13(6):e1002165, 2015) to over 200 billion USD per year worldwide (Chalmers and Glasziou in Lancet 374:86-89, 2009).

findings.claim: A six-centre preclinical randomized controlled trial (pRCT) of anti-CD49d antibodies for stroke confirmed benefit only in small cortical infarcts and no benefit in large lesions, showing efficacy is model-dependent even though a clinical trial had already been launched on conflicting single-lab data.
findings.claim_source_sentence: In contrast, anti-CD49d treatment did not reduce lesion size or affect leukocyte invasion after transient proximal occlusion of the middle cerebral artery, which induces large lesions.
findings.evidence: Centrally coordinated, randomized, blinded pRCT across six independent European centres in two mouse stroke models, undertaken after four positive and one inconclusive single-lab studies had triggered a clinical trial.
findings.effect_size: benefit only in small cortical (distal MCAO) infarcts; no effect in large (transient proximal MCAO) lesions
findings.effect_size_source_sentence: These results suggest that the benefits of immune-targeted approaches may depend on infarct severity and localization.

findings.claim: A meta-analysis of 21 animal studies found MSC-derived small extracellular vesicles significantly accelerate type II diabetic wound healing (SMD 3.16), but the authors stress the evidence remains limited to preclinical models.
findings.claim_source_sentence: Twenty-one studies were included in this meta-analysis. Compared with the control group, MSC-sEVs were found to significantly facilitate the healing of cutaneous wounds in type II diabetic patients (standardized mean difference [SMD]=3.16, 95% confidence interval [CI]: 2.65 to 3.66, P<0.00001, I39%).
findings.evidence: Systematic review and meta-analysis using the SYRCLE risk-of-bias tool; PROSPERO-registered; wound closure primary outcome.
findings.effect_size: wound closure SMD 3.16 (95% CI 2.65-3.66); 21 studies
findings.effect_size_source_sentence: Twenty-one studies were included in this meta-analysis. Compared with the control group, MSC-sEVs were found to significantly facilitate the healing of cutaneous wounds in type II diabetic patients (standardized mean difference [SMD]=3.16, 95% confidence interval [CI]: 2.65 to 3.66, P<0.00001, I39%).
findings.study_system: animal models of type II diabetic cutaneous wounds (MSC-sEVs)

findings.claim: A meta-analysis of MSC-derived extracellular vesicles for diabetic wounds pooled only 10 studies (136 animals) with a very large apparent effect (SMD 5.48) but unclear risk of bias across all included studies.
findings.claim_source_sentence: The administration of MSC-EVs improved closure of diabetic wounds compared to controls with a large observed effect (Standardized Mean Difference (SMD) 5.48, 95% Confidence Interval (CI) 3.55-8.13).
findings.evidence: Systematic review and random-effects meta-analysis using the SYRCLE risk-of-bias tool; 10 studies, 136 animals; PROSPERO-registered.
findings.effect_size: wound closure SMD 5.48 (95% CI 3.55-8.13); risk of bias unclear across studies
findings.effect_size_source_sentence: ROB across studies was unclear.

findings.claim: Inconsistent antibody performance is a major driver of irreproducibility; the lack of accepted validation standards causes Western blot and other immunoassay results to vary widely between laboratories.
findings.claim_source_sentence: Well-characterized antibody reagents play a key role in the reproducibility of research findings, and inconsistent antibody performance leads to variability in Western blotting and other immunoassays.
findings.evidence: Methodology paper proposing practical strategies for validating primary-antibody specificity, selectivity and reproducibility in Western blotting, with orthogonal-method confirmation.

findings.claim: Misuse of immunohistochemistry contributes to the reproducibility crisis: over 3.8 million 'research-grade' antibodies are commercialized largely without extensive validation, versus fewer than 500 highly validated clinical-grade diagnostic antibodies.
findings.claim_source_sentence: The other main class of antibodies are "research grade" antibodies (now numbering >3 800 000), which are often not extensively validated prior to commercialization.
findings.evidence: Review of common IHC assay pitfalls with case vignettes, arguing end-users must validate antibodies in their own laboratories regardless of manufacturer claims.
findings.effect_size: >3,800,000 unvalidated research-grade antibodies vs <500 validated clinical-grade
findings.effect_size_source_sentence: Such diagnostic antibodies, which tend to be highly validated prior to clinical implementation, are in the vast minority ( < 500).

findings.claim: To address the reproducibility crisis, an NIH program generated 1,406 rigorously validated, renewable monoclonal antibodies against 737 human transcription factors through an integrated production and validation pipeline.
findings.claim_source_sentence: As part of the US National Institutes of Health (NIH) Protein Capture Reagents Program (PCRP), we have generated a collection of 1,406 highly validated immunoprecipitation- and/or immunoblotting-grade mouse monoclonal antibodies (mAbs) to 737 human transcription factors, using an integrated production and validation pipeline.
findings.evidence: Antibody-generation study using HuProt human protein microarrays as primary validation plus immunoprecipitation, immunoblotting, ChIP-seq and immunohistochemistry.
findings.effect_size: 1,406 validated mAbs to 737 transcription factors
findings.effect_size_source_sentence: As part of the US National Institutes of Health (NIH) Protein Capture Reagents Program (PCRP), we have generated a collection of 1,406 highly validated immunoprecipitation- and/or immunoblotting-grade mouse monoclonal antibodies (mAbs) to 737 human transcription factors, using an integrated production and validation pipeline.

findings.claim: A systematic review of preclinical guidelines identified 26 documents (most for neurological/cerebrovascular drugs) offering 55 recommendations to counter the internal, construct and external validity threats behind the dismal clinical success rate.
findings.claim_source_sentence: From these, we identified 26 guidelines that met our eligibility criteria--most of which were directed at neurological or cerebrovascular drug development.
findings.evidence: Systematic review of 2,029 citations yielding 26 preclinical guideline documents, with recommendations organised by validity-threat type.
findings.effect_size: 26 guidelines; 55 recommendations (from 2,029 citations screened)
findings.effect_size_source_sentence: Together, these guidelines offered 55 different recommendations.
findings.study_system: preclinical in vivo efficacy guidelines (systematic review)

findings.claim: In a meta-analysis of 503 animal studies, ischaemic preconditioning reduced myocardial infarction 24.6%, but randomization, blinding and sample-size calculation were reported in only 49%, 11% and 2% of publications.
findings.claim_source_sentence: Reporting of study quality indicators was low: randomization, blinding and a sample size calculation were reported in 49%, 11% and 2% of publications, respectively.
findings.evidence: Systematic review and meta-analysis of 785 IPC-vs-control comparisons from 503 animal myocardial-infarction studies, with subgroup and quality analysis.
findings.effect_size: IPC reduced infarction 24.6% (95%CI 23.5-25.6); quality reporting 49%/11%/2%
findings.effect_size_source_sentence: Overall, IPC reduced myocardial infarction by 24.6% [95%CI 23.5, 25.6].

findings.claim: A meta-analysis of preclinical sunitinib studies found no experiment used blinded outcome assessment, most malignancies were tested in only one model, and effect sizes were inflated ~45% by potential publication bias.
findings.claim_source_sentence: We calculate a 45% overestimate of effect size across all malignancies due to potential publication bias.
findings.evidence: Extraction of tumour-volume effect sizes from published sunitinib monotherapy animal experiments against internal/external validity criteria.
findings.effect_size: 45% effect-size overestimate; 0% studies with blinded assessment
findings.effect_size_source_sentence: We calculate a 45% overestimate of effect size across all malignancies due to potential publication bias.

findings.claim: A meta-analysis of 39 renal ischaemia-reperfusion studies (>250 control, >290 treated animals) found ischaemic postconditioning ameliorates injury, but bias-reduction measures were insufficiently reported and studies used almost exclusively young, healthy, male animals.
findings.claim_source_sentence: Measures to reduce bias were insufficiently reported.
findings.evidence: Systematic review, quality assessment and meta-analysis of preclinical renal ischaemic postconditioning across 39 publications.
findings.effect_size: 39 publications; >250 control + >290 IPoC animals
findings.effect_size_source_sentence: We identified 39 publications studying >250 control animals undergoing renal IRI only and >290 animals undergoing renal IRI and IPoC.

findings.claim: In a systematic review of 23 animal knee-osteoarthritis MSC studies, all had high risk of bias per SYRCLE and evidence quality was low or very low, so clinical translation could not be recommended.
findings.claim_source_sentence: According to the SYRCLE's tool, all included studies had high risk of bias.
findings.evidence: SYRCLE-assessed systematic review of 23 preclinical intra-articular MSC studies for knee osteoarthritis with CERQual evidence grading.
findings.effect_size: 23 studies; all high risk of bias; evidence low/very low
findings.effect_size_source_sentence: Twenty-three KOA animal studies were eligible for inclusion.
findings.study_system: animal knee osteoarthritis MSC injection (systematic review)

findings.claim: A SYRCLE-assessed meta-analysis of 15 rodent stroke studies reported metformin significantly improved every endpoint (e.g. infarct size, neurological score), the same near-universal positive pattern that characterises publication-biased preclinical literature.
findings.claim_source_sentence: Overall, metformin treatment improves severe outcomes triggered by stroke.
findings.evidence: Meta-analysis of 15 rodent stroke trials (2010-2022) with SYRCLE risk-of-bias assessment reporting standardized mean differences across eight endpoints.
findings.effect_size: 15 studies; all eight endpoints significant (e.g. infarct SMD -2.90)
findings.effect_size_source_sentence: Fifteen articles published from 2010 to 2022 were included in the meta-analysis.

findings.claim: A GRADE-rated meta-analysis of 70 preclinical electroacupuncture stroke studies documented major methodological limitations: only 4 studies had low risk of allocation concealment and 9 had high risk of randomization bias.
findings.claim_source_sentence: However, several methodological limitations were identified: only 4 studies demonstrated a low risk of allocation concealment, 26 achieved a low risk of outcome assessment bias, and 9 had a high risk of randomization bias.
findings.evidence: Systematic review and random-effects meta-analysis (Hedge's g) of 70 electroacupuncture ischaemic-stroke studies with GRADE evidence rating.
findings.effect_size: 70 studies; 4 low-risk allocation concealment; 9 high-risk randomization; 12 outcomes moderate / 6 low quality (GRADE)
findings.effect_size_source_sentence: Data from 70 eligible studies were analyzed in Stata 18.0, using a random-effects model to calculate the standardized mean difference (Hedge's g).

findings.claim: A meta-analysis of 19 animal stroke studies of intra-arterial cooling found consistent benefit (infarct reduction 23.67%) but all used young, healthy animals and sample-size calculations were infrequent, with median methodological quality of 5/12.
findings.claim_source_sentence: Some experimental design elements, such as blinding, were common whereas others, such as sample size calculations, were infrequent (median methodological quality score: 5; range: 2-7).
findings.evidence: PRISMA systematic review and meta-analysis of 19 intra-arterial selective cooling-infusion stroke studies scored on a 0-12 methodological-quality scale.
findings.effect_size: infarct volume reduction 23.67% (95% CI 19.21-28.12); median quality 5/12
findings.effect_size_source_sentence: Our analyses revealed that IA-SCI provides benefit on all endpoints (mean normalized infarct volume reduction = 23.67%; 95% CI: 19.21-28.12; mean normalized behavioral improvement = 35.56%; 95% CI: 25.91-45.20; mean standardized edema reduction = 0.95; 95% CI: 0.56-1.34).

findings.claim: Creatine was neuroprotective in animal Parkinson's models and advanced to trials, but a meta-analysis of 3 RCTs (n=1935) found no benefit on any UPDRS outcome, a clear preclinical-to-clinical translational failure.
findings.claim_source_sentence: Creatine is an antioxidant agent that showed neuroprotective effects in animal models of Parkinson's disease (PD).
findings.evidence: PRISMA meta-analysis of three randomized placebo-controlled creatine trials pooling UPDRS outcomes; no significant difference on total or subscale scores.
findings.effect_size: 3 RCTs, n=1935; UPDRS total MD 1.07 (95% CI 3.38 to 1.25), no benefit
findings.effect_size_source_sentence: Three RCTs (n=1935) were included in this study.
findings.study_system: creatine, Parkinson's disease (animal models vs clinical RCTs)

findings.claim: Over 300 interventions reportedly mitigated Alzheimer's pathology or behaviour in animal models, yet very few achieved human target validation or disease-modifying therapies, partly due to under-reporting of negative results.
findings.claim_source_sentence: As a result, over 300 interventions have been investigated and reported to mitigate pathological phenotypes or improve behavior in AD animal models or both.
findings.evidence: Expert advisory-panel consensus on best practices for preclinical Alzheimer's animal studies, citing publication bias and lack of design standards as translation barriers.
findings.effect_size: >300 interventions effective in AD animal models; very few translated
findings.effect_size_source_sentence: As a result, over 300 interventions have been investigated and reported to mitigate pathological phenotypes or improve behavior in AD animal models or both.

findings.claim: Despite initiatives on internal validity and reporting (ARRIVE, PREPARE), progress on the external validity of animal disease models has been virtually absent; the authors propose a Framework to Identify Models of Disease (FIMD) to standardise predictive-value assessment.
findings.claim_source_sentence: As for external validity, progress has been virtually absent.
findings.evidence: Perspective introducing FIMD plus systematic-review and Investigator's-Brochure-derisk approaches to evaluate animal-model translatability.

findings.claim: Systematic reviews of cardiovascular animal studies reveal serious internal- and external-validity limitations that, with inter-species differences, undermine the predictive value of animal research for new drug efficacy and tolerability.
findings.claim_source_sentence: Systematic reviews of animal studies have revealed serious limitations in internal and external validity strongly affecting the reliability of this research.
findings.evidence: Review of translational barriers in cardiovascular pharmacotherapy, calling for improved lab/publication practices and early human proof-of-concept studies.

findings.claim: A systematic review of 34 studies found ALS animal models reproduce human ALS neuroimaging features (high external validity), yet drug attrition remains high, showing that phenotypic reproducibility does not make a model fit for drug development.
findings.claim_source_sentence: This opposes the high attrition of drugs during bench-to-bedside translation and thus raises concerns that phenotypic reproducibility does not necessarily render an animal model appropriate for drug development.
findings.evidence: PROSPERO-registered systematic review of MRI features in ALS/MND animal models with risk-of-bias assessment.
findings.effect_size: 201 publications screened; 34 eligible
findings.effect_size_source_sentence: In a comprehensive literature search in PubMed and Embase, we retrieved 201 unique publications of which 34 were deemed eligible for qualitative synthesis including risk of bias assessment.

findings.claim: A systematic review found preclinical WEB-device aneurysm testing relied on a single animal model (rabbit elastase), never reported safety outcomes, and showed more heterogeneous efficacy than clinical studies, limiting external validity.
findings.claim_source_sentence: Safety outcomes were not evaluated in animal studies and could therefore not be compared to clinical outcomes.
findings.evidence: SYRCLE/Newcastle-Ottawa systematic review comparing 6 animal and 17 clinical WEB-device studies.
findings.effect_size: 6 animal studies vs 17 clinical studies; 1 animal model used
findings.effect_size_source_sentence: Six animal studies and 17 clinical studies met the inclusion criteria.
findings.study_system: intracranial aneurysm WEB device (animal vs clinical systematic review)

findings.claim: A systematic review of 13 studies concluded colorectal-cancer patient-derived xenografts have reasonable internal and high external validity (median engraftment 70%), but reporting standards need standardisation to ARRIVE.
findings.claim_source_sentence: Thirteen articles satisfied the inclusion criteria.
findings.evidence: PRISMA/SYRCLE systematic review of validated colorectal-cancer PDX models across multiple parameters.
findings.effect_size: 13 studies; median engraftment rate 70%
findings.effect_size_source_sentence: There was significant heterogeneity amongst the included studies, but overall the median engraftment rate was high (70%) and PDX models faithfully recapitulated the characteristics of their patient tumours on the microscopic, genetic and functional levels.

findings.claim: Genetic background strongly influences xenograft development and phenotype; the authors argue a diverse, well-characterised ecosystem of mouse models is needed to address the reproducibility and translatability crises in preclinical cancer research.
findings.claim_source_sentence: In a recent study, Sargent et al. characterise several novel Rag1-/- mouse strains and demonstrate that genetic background strongly influences xenograft development and phenotype.
findings.evidence: Commentary situating strain-dependent xenograft variability within reproducibility/translatability crises and advocating deliberate biological-variation re-introduction.

findings.claim: Pluripotent stem-cell lines derived from different mouse strains showed divergent differentiation capacity, confirming that genetic background plays a dominant role in PSC phenotypic variability that hampers experimental reproducibility.
findings.claim_source_sentence: Overall, this study shows that genetic background plays a dominant role in driving phenotypic variability of PSCs.
findings.evidence: Derivation of PSCs from distinct mouse strains under naive conditions showing genotype-driven differences in differentiation and Wnt signalling.

findings.claim: In standardized behavioural assays across two genetic backgrounds, a single retest of a P<0.05 result reproduced only 60% of the time, and sampling variation was the largest confound masking genetic-background effects.
findings.claim_source_sentence: The reproducibility and robustness of phenotypic measures has become a concern that undermines the use of mouse genetic models for translational studies.
findings.evidence: Statistically robust reanalysis of three mutations on 129S5 and C57BL/6J backgrounds across five standardized behavioural assays.
findings.effect_size: single-retest reproducibility ~60% at P<0.05
findings.effect_size_source_sentence: We determined that, for frequently used group sizes, a single retest of a significant result conforming to the commonly used P < 0.05 threshold results in a reproducibility of 60% between identical experiments.
findings.study_system: mutant mouse behaviour (129S5 and C57BL/6J backgrounds)

findings.claim: Analysis of Mouse Phenome Database datasets showed behavioural tests had high coefficients of variation (0.4-0.6 or higher) versus below 0.25 for most clinical-chemistry parameters, demonstrating unpredictable genotype-environment-experiment interactions affecting reproducibility.
findings.claim_source_sentence: The behavioral tests showed a CV between 0.4 and 0.6, or higher.
findings.evidence: Variability analysis of clinical-chemical, haematological, immunological and behavioural parameters across Mouse Phenome Database projects for commonly used strains.
findings.effect_size: behavioural CV 0.4-0.6+; most clinical-chemistry CV <0.25
findings.effect_size_source_sentence: Most of the clinical chemical and hematological parameters-except of some parameters being known for their high variability-showed an average coefficient of variation (CV = standard deviation / mean) below 0.25.
findings.study_system: laboratory mouse phenotypic parameters (Mouse Phenome Database)

findings.claim: Unlike chemical reagents, mice have an intrinsic genetic drive to change, with mutations accumulating over time that compromise the reproducibility of experimental data over time and place.
findings.claim_source_sentence: Such changes compromise the reproducibility of experimental data over time and place.
findings.evidence: Review of sources of genetic drift in inbred mice and strategies (international genetic standards) to reduce them.

findings.claim: After 12 weeks, corncob versus paper bedding produced significant differences in the gut microbiome of mice on both normal and high-fat diets, demonstrating that husbandry details influence the reproducibility of dietary-obesity research.
findings.claim_source_sentence: After 12 wk, the GM showed significant differences depending on both bedding and diet.
findings.evidence: Controlled comparison of paper vs corncob bedding effects on weight, metabolism and 16S-sequenced faecal/cecal microbiomes in C57BL/6J mice.
findings.study_system: C57BL/6J mice, bedding and diet (gut microbiome)

findings.claim: Lifetime exposure to different standard chow diets made genetically identical mice differ significantly in growth and show nine times more differentially abundant gut bacterial genera, identifying chow and exposure timing as major sources of preclinical variability.
findings.claim_source_sentence: Our findings demonstrate that LE to different chow diets has the greatest impact on the reproducibility of several experimental measures commonly used in preclinical mouse model studies.
findings.evidence: Factorial study of four chow diets across adult, lifetime and developmental exposure windows in C57BL/6J mice measuring growth, metabolic and 16S microbiome outcomes.
findings.effect_size: lifetime-exposure mice: 9x more differentially abundant bacterial genera
findings.effect_size_source_sentence: However, compared with AE, LE effects on beta diversity were sex dependent, and LE mice exhibited nine times more differentially abundant bacterial genera, the majority of which were inversely affected by 2920X and 5058 diets.
findings.study_system: C57BL/6J mice, chow diet timing (gut microbiota)

findings.claim: A systematic review of 128 meniscus-repair animal studies found that, lacking guidance documentation, preclinical models are not performed in a standardized fashion, and a Best Practices document would increase reproducibility and external validity.
findings.claim_source_sentence: However, given the current lack of guidance documentation in this area, preclinical animal models are not performed in a standardized fashion.
findings.evidence: PRISMA systematic review of 128 meniscus animal-model studies scored against predefined study descriptors and outcome measures.
findings.effect_size: 128 studies; rabbit 46%, dog 21%, sheep 20%
findings.effect_size_source_sentence: A total of 128 full-length peer-reviewed manuscripts were identified.

findings.claim: Despite hundreds of preclinical successes, no intervention has confirmed efficacy in Alzheimer's clinical trials, a failure the MODEL-AD consortium attributes partly to the animal models, the assays used, and lack of scientific rigor and reproducibility during execution.
findings.claim_source_sentence: Critically this lack of translation to the clinic points in part to issues with the animal models, the preclinical assays used, and lack of scientific rigor and reproducibility during execution.
findings.evidence: Description of the MODEL-AD Preclinical Testing Core rigorous go/no-go screening pipeline with QC checkpoints and ARRIVE-aligned design.

findings.claim: Meta-research estimates that roughly 85% of biomedical research resources are wasted; the paper argues for transplanting replication, registration, sharing and reward-system reforms across fields to raise the proportion of true findings.
findings.claim_source_sentence: Currently, an estimated 85% of research resources are wasted.
findings.evidence: Ioannidis perspective on meta-research and interventions to improve credibility/efficiency of science (body: Effective Interventions).
findings.effect_size: ~85% of research resources wasted
findings.effect_size_source_sentence: Currently, an estimated 85% of research resources are wasted.

findings.claim: A meta-analysis of 311 rat neuroscience studies found female rats are not more variable than males across behavioral, electrophysiological, neurochemical and histological measures, even at defined estrous-cycle stages, undercutting a common justification for excluding females.
findings.claim_source_sentence: Across a substantially large sampling of research, the data indicate that on average, females exhibit the same (or less) variability on a given trait that male rats do.
findings.evidence: Coefficient-of-variation meta-analysis across 311 articles and >6000 data points per sex (body: Conclusions).
findings.effect_size: 311 articles; >6000 data points per sex; no main effect of sex on CV
findings.effect_size_source_sentence: Only empirical articles using both male and female gonad-intact adult rats, written in English, and describing the number of subjects (or a range) were included—resulting in 311 articles for analysis.
findings.study_system: male and female rats, neuroscience traits (meta-analysis)

findings.claim: A survey on rodent age in research found most studies use animals 8-12 weeks old with a wide range (2-120 weeks) and vague age justifications (11.5% simply said 'adult'), highlighting inconsistent reporting of a variable that affects study outcomes and reproducibility.
findings.claim_source_sentence: The majority of responses described using animals between eight and 12 weeks, with a range from two to 120 weeks of age.
findings.evidence: Survey of rodent researchers on age selection and its justification (body: Results).
findings.effect_size: age range 2-120 weeks; 11.5% justified age as 'adult'
findings.effect_size_source_sentence: Responses (11.5%) cited that the reason for the choice of age was the rodent being 'adult'.

findings.claim: A manifesto for reproducible science documents that statistical power in many fields persistently sits below 50%, and that outcome-reporting infidelity is severe, with only 13% of trials publishing outcomes fully consistent with their pre-registered commitments.
findings.claim_source_sentence: Studies of statistical power persistently find it to be below (sometimes well below) 50%, across both time and the different disciplines studied.
findings.evidence: Synthesis of threats to reproducibility across the research lifecycle (body: Methods / Reporting and dissemination sections).
findings.effect_size: statistical power <50%; only 13% of trials fully consistent with pre-registration
findings.effect_size_source_sentence: one study observed that just 13% of trials published outcomes completely consistent with the pre-registered commitments.

findings.claim: A GBSI economic analysis estimated that more than half of preclinical research is irreproducible, with associated costs of about $28 billion per year in the United States alone.
findings.claim_source_sentence: Based on these findings, GBSI completed an economic study in 2015 and estimated that the prevalence of irreproducible preclinical research exceeds 50%, with associated annual costs of approximately $28B in the United States alone.
findings.evidence: Reproducibility2020 progress report restating the GBSI/Freedman economic estimate (body: Introduction).
findings.effect_size: >50% preclinical research irreproducible; ~$28B/year in the US
findings.effect_size_source_sentence: Based on these findings, GBSI completed an economic study in 2015 and estimated that the prevalence of irreproducible preclinical research exceeds 50%, with associated annual costs of approximately $28B in the United States alone.

findings.claim: A post-mortem of the failed Phase III progesterone traumatic brain injury trials attributes translational failure partly to insensitive clinical outcome instruments that do not match the precision of the morphological and functional endpoints used in the supporting animal studies.
findings.claim_source_sentence: the great majority of them use the same standardized, short, blunt instruments evaluating quality-of-life that do not approach the detail and precision of the measures used to evaluate morphological and functional outcomes required of animal studies
findings.evidence: Analysis of why preclinically-supported progesterone failed in Phase III TBI trials (body: Outcome measures section).
findings.study_system: traumatic brain injury (progesterone Phase III trials, translational analysis)

findings.claim: Metaresearch on reproducibility in ecology and evolution notes that only 39% of replications in a large replication project reproduced the original results, with replication effect sizes averaging only half those of the originals.
findings.claim_source_sentence: Only 39% of replications reproduced the results of the original studies, with replication effect sizes averaging only half those of the originals.
findings.evidence: Review of reproducibility metrics applied to ecology/evolution, citing large-scale replication data (body: Evaluating the reproducibility of scientific results).
findings.effect_size: 39% of replications reproduced; replication effect sizes ~half of originals
findings.effect_size_source_sentence: Only 39% of replications reproduced the results of the original studies, with replication effect sizes averaging only half those of the originals.
findings.study_system: ecology and evolution meta-research (citing replication project)

findings.claim: In a survey of in vivo researchers on scientific rigor, self-reported use of bias-control measures was uneven: 69% reported sample-size calculation and 52% allocation concealment, but fewer than half (47%) reported blinded outcome assessment.
findings.claim_source_sentence: More than half also ticked sample size calculation (69%, N = 203) and allocation concealment (52%, N = 143), whereas less than half (47%, N = 135) ticked blinded outcome assessment.
findings.evidence: Researchers' self-reported rigor practices survey (body: Measures to avoid bias).
findings.effect_size: sample-size calculation 69%; allocation concealment 52%; blinded outcome assessment 47%
findings.effect_size_source_sentence: More than half also ticked sample size calculation (69%, N = 203) and allocation concealment (52%, N = 143), whereas less than half (47%, N = 135) ticked blinded outcome assessment.
findings.study_system: survey of in vivo researchers (rigor practices)

findings.claim: A nationwide analysis of preclinical animal publications found reporting of random allocation rose from 24.0% (2009) to 40.8% (2018), and conflict-of-interest reporting from 37.6% to 90.4%, indicating improvement but persistent underreporting of key bias safeguards.
findings.claim_source_sentence: Random allocation of animals to experimental groups was reported in 60 publications (24.0%, CI 18.8–29.8%) from 2009 (out of 234 in which this would have been appropriate; 93.6%), which increased to 102 publications (40.8%, CI 34.7–47.2%) in 2018 (out of 233 in which this would have been appropriate; 93.2%).
findings.evidence: Nationwide systematic investigation comparing reporting quality of preclinical animal research in 2009 vs 2018 (body: Part I: The overall reporting status).
findings.effect_size: randomization reporting 24.0%→40.8%; conflict-of-interest reporting 37.6%→90.4%
findings.effect_size_source_sentence: The reporting on conflicts of interest increased from 94 publications (37.6%, CI 31.6–43.9%) in 2009 to 226 publications (90.4%, CI 86.1–93.8%) in 2018.

findings.claim: A meta-commentary on preclinical systematic reviews found study quality is uniformly low: no CAMARADES-rated review scored any included study above 8 out of 10 (median 4/10), and only 55% of the reviews assessed publication bias.
findings.claim_source_sentence: No review using the CAMARADES quality rating scored a single included publication higher than 8 out of 10, with the median score being 4.
findings.evidence: Commentary analysing 20 preclinical systematic reviews for quality and publication-bias assessment (body: Lesson 5 / Lesson 6).
findings.effect_size: median CAMARADES quality 4/10 (max 8/10); 55% of reviews assessed publication bias
findings.effect_size_source_sentence: Of the 20 studies we analysed for this commentary, only 11 (55%) considered publication bias.

findings.claim: A preclinical meta-analysis conducted before a first-in-human trial found mesenchymal stem cell therapy sharply reduced mortality in rodent sepsis models (OR 0.27, 95% CI 0.18-0.40), but internal validity was weak, with only 45% of experiments reporting randomization and none describing sequence generation.
findings.claim_source_sentence: Forty-five percent of experiments reported that the animals were randomized, none described methods of sequence generation
findings.evidence: Systematic review and meta-analysis of 20 controlled MSC sepsis experiments (980 animals) with risk-of-bias assessment (body: Results).
findings.effect_size: mortality OR 0.27 (95% CI 0.18-0.40); 45% reported randomization
findings.effect_size_source_sentence: MSC therapy in preclinical models of sepsis significantly reduced the overall odds of death (odds ratio (OR) 0.27, 95% confidence interval (CI) 0.18–0.40
findings.study_system: mesenchymal stem cells in rodent sepsis models (20 experiments, 980 animals)

findings.claim: A machine-assisted systematic review of 337 animal studies of chemotherapy-induced peripheral neuropathy found bias safeguards were rarely reported (only 28.5% reported randomisation, 51.3% blinded outcome assessment) and trim-and-fill imputed 316 theoretically missing studies, indicating severe publication bias.
findings.claim_source_sentence: 51.3% (n = 173) reported blinded assessment of outcome, 28.5% (n = 96) reported randomisation to group
findings.evidence: Machine-assisted systematic review and meta-analysis of CIPN animal models with risk-of-bias and publication-bias analysis (body: Results).
findings.effect_size: randomisation reported 28.5%; blinded outcome 51.3%; 316 missing studies imputed
findings.effect_size_source_sentence: Trim and fill analysis imputed 316 theoretical missing studies on the right-hand side of the funnel plot
findings.study_system: animal models of chemotherapy-induced peripheral neuropathy (machine-assisted systematic review)

findings.claim: A systematic review and meta-analysis of stem cell transplantation in animal spinal cord injury found a ~27.2% improvement in motor outcome across 312 comparisons in 5,628 animals, but randomization and blinded outcome assessment were each reported in only 46% of publications.
findings.claim_source_sentence: Random allocation to treatment group (72, 46%) and blinded assessment of outcome (72, 46%) were reported more frequently in these publications than in the modelling of other neurological disorders.
findings.evidence: Meta-analysis of allogeneic stem cell therapy in animal SCI models with risk-of-bias assessment (body: Results).
findings.effect_size: motor improvement 27.2% (95% CI 25.0-29.4%); randomization/blinding each 46%
findings.effect_size_source_sentence: Overall, allogeneic stem cell treatment appears to improve both motor (effect size, 27.2%; 95% Confidence Interval [CI], 25.0%–29.4%; 312 comparisons in 5,628 animals) and sensory (effect size, 26.3%; 95% CI, 7.9%–44.7%; 23 comparisons in 473 animals) outcome.
findings.study_system: allogeneic stem cell transplantation in animal spinal cord injury models (312 comparisons, 5628 animals)

findings.claim: A systematic review and meta-analysis of animal ischaemic stroke studies found that hyperthermia/fever substantially worsens outcome, increasing infarct size by 43.4%.
findings.claim_source_sentence: Hyperthermia increased infarct size by 43.4% (95% CI, 29.8% to 56.9%)
findings.evidence: Meta-analysis of 19 publications (49 comparisons, 603 animals) on fever and stroke outcome (body: Results).
findings.effect_size: infarct size increased 43.4% (95% CI 29.8-56.9%)
findings.effect_size_source_sentence: Hyperthermia increased infarct size by 43.4% (95% CI, 29.8% to 56.9%)
findings.study_system: animal models of ischaemic stroke (fever/hyperthermia; 19 publications, 603 animals)

findings.claim: A preclinical systematic review and meta-analysis of 32 studies found the noble gas argon reduced combined histologic and neurological injury by 18.1% in animal models of acquired brain injury.
findings.claim_source_sentence: Argon was found to reduce neurological injury (combined histologic and neurological deficits) by 18.1% (95% CI, 8.1–28.1%; Z=3.6; P<0.001).
findings.evidence: Preclinical systematic review and meta-analysis of argon and xenon neuroprotection (body: Results).
findings.effect_size: argon reduced neurological injury by 18.1% (95% CI 8.1-28.1%)
findings.effect_size_source_sentence: Argon was found to reduce neurological injury (combined histologic and neurological deficits) by 18.1% (95% CI, 8.1–28.1%; Z=3.6; P<0.001).
findings.study_system: argon and xenon neuroprotection in animal acquired brain injury models (32 studies)

findings.claim: A systematic review of 374 animal studies of cannabinoids for pain found bias safeguards were seldom reported, with only 32% reporting randomisation and 47% reporting blinded outcome assessment.
findings.claim_source_sentence: 47% (175) reported blinded assessment of outcome, 32% (118) reported randomisation (to treatment or control group)
findings.evidence: Systematic review and meta-analysis of cannabinoid antinociception in animal models with risk-of-bias assessment (body: 4.7 Risk of Bias).
findings.effect_size: randomisation reported 32%; blinded outcome assessment 47% (of 374 studies)
findings.effect_size_source_sentence: 47% (175) reported blinded assessment of outcome, 32% (118) reported randomisation (to treatment or control group)
findings.study_system: animal models of cannabinoid antinociception (systematic review)

findings.claim: A preclinical systematic review of topoisomerase inhibition in glioma models found treated animals survived 1.32 times longer than controls, but with extreme between-study heterogeneity (I2 = 92.2%) and only modest study quality (median 6 of 12 checklist items).
findings.claim_source_sentence: The study quality was modest, the median number of checklist items scored 6 out of 12 (IQR – 5–7, range 3–9).
findings.evidence: Systematic review and meta-analysis of topoisomerase inhibitors in preclinical glioma models (body: Results).
findings.effect_size: survival ratio 1.32 (95% CI 1.23-1.43); I2 = 92.2%; median quality 6/12
findings.effect_size_source_sentence: Overall, animals bearing gliomas treated with a topoisomerase inhibitor survived 1.32 times (95% CI: 1.23 – 1.43) longer than control animals, substantial between-study heterogeneity was observed (F = 7.1, p < 0.001, I² = 92.2%).
findings.study_system: preclinical glioma models, topoisomerase inhibitors (systematic review)

findings.claim: A methodological review found that more than 20 different risk-of-bias/quality-appraisal tools have been developed for medical studies, a proliferation that undermines standardization of how study quality is judged.
findings.claim_source_sentence: Until now there were more than 20 appraisal tools have been developed.
findings.evidence: Review comparing risk-of-bias assessment tools for primary and secondary medical studies (body: Discussion and conclusions).
findings.effect_size: >20 appraisal tools developed
findings.effect_size_source_sentence: Until now there were more than 20 appraisal tools have been developed.
findings.study_system: methodological review of risk-of-bias/quality assessment tools

findings.claim: Despite thousands of experimental cardioprotection studies, only one has unequivocally translated to improved clinical outcome as a primary endpoint, a failure the authors attribute to lack of rigor/reproducibility in preclinical studies and poor clinical trial design.
findings.claim_source_sentence: so far there is only a single and very recent study, which has unequivocally translated cardioprotection to improved clinical outcome as the primary endpoint in patients
findings.evidence: Practical guidelines noting the cardioprotection translation gap and its causes (body: Introduction).

findings.claim: A systematic review of rodent burrowing as a pain outcome found methodological-quality reporting was generally low: only 14% reported allocation concealment, 43% blinded outcome assessment, and 38% sample-size calculation, even though random-allocation reporting was relatively high (70%).
findings.claim_source_sentence: The reporting of other methodological quality criteria was low: 14% reported allocation concealment, 43% reported blinding of outcome assessment, 38% reported sample size calculation, 41% reported predefined animal inclusion criteria, and 36% reported animal exclusions.
findings.evidence: Systematic review and meta-analysis of burrowing behaviour in rodent pain models with risk-of-bias assessment (body: 3.4 Risk of bias).
findings.effect_size: allocation concealment 14%; blinded outcome 43%; sample-size calculation 38%; random allocation 70%
findings.effect_size_source_sentence: The reporting of other methodological quality criteria was low: 14% reported allocation concealment, 43% reported blinding of outcome assessment, 38% reported sample size calculation, 41% reported predefined animal inclusion criteria, and 36% reported animal exclusions.
findings.study_system: rodent pain models with burrowing outcome (systematic review)

findings.claim: The preclinical literature is expanding faster than systematic review can keep pace: a single neuropathic-pain search rose from 6,506 articles (2012) to 12,614 (2015), versus only 129 clinical trials identified, motivating automated meta-research tools.
findings.claim_source_sentence: For example, in preclinical neuropathic pain research, the number of articles retrieved by a systematic search rose from 6506 in 2012 to 12 614 in 2015 whereas comparatively, only 129 neuropathic pain clinical trials were identified.
findings.evidence: Review of technological/automation advances in preclinical meta-research (body: Introduction).
findings.effect_size: 6506 (2012) to 12,614 (2015) preclinical articles vs 129 clinical trials
findings.effect_size_source_sentence: For example, in preclinical neuropathic pain research, the number of articles retrieved by a systematic search rose from 6506 in 2012 to 12 614 in 2015 whereas comparatively, only 129 neuropathic pain clinical trials were identified.
findings.study_system: preclinical neuropathic pain literature (meta-research on automation)

findings.claim: Failure to analyze sex in research carries clinical consequences: of the ten prescription drugs withdrawn from the US market between 1997 and 2001, eight caused greater harm to women than to men, motivating sex-disaggregated reporting standards.
findings.claim_source_sentence: Among the ten prescription pharmaceuticals withdrawn from the US market between 1997 and 2001, eight caused greater harm to women than men.
findings.evidence: Rationale for the SAGER sex/gender reporting guidelines (body: Sex and gender bias in the conduct of research).
findings.effect_size: 8 of 10 withdrawn drugs harmed women more than men
findings.effect_size_source_sentence: Among the ten prescription pharmaceuticals withdrawn from the US market between 1997 and 2001, eight caused greater harm to women than men.
findings.study_system: sex/gender reporting in biomedical research (SAGER guidelines rationale)

findings.claim: A meta-analysis of 49 preclinical studies found neutrophil contribution to pain depends on the pain model, outcome and depletion method, with commonly used depletion strategies (anti-neutrophil serum, anti-Gr-1) producing weaker effects than others.
findings.claim_source_sentence: In conclusion, the contribution of neutrophils to pain depends on pain etiology (experimental model), pain outcome, and the neutrophil depletion strategy.
findings.evidence: Systematic review and meta-analysis (PROSPERO CRD42022364004) of 49 preclinical studies with SYRCLE risk-of-bias assessment; effects varied by model, outcome and method.
findings.effect_size: 49 studies; medium-large effect sizes but method-dependent
findings.effect_size_source_sentence: Inflammatory, joint, neuropathic, and visceral pain showed significant pain alleviation by neutrophil depletion with medium-large effect sizes.

findings.claim: A meta-analysis of 11 exosome-for-diabetic-neuropathy studies reported large pooled benefits but with unclear risk of bias in most studies and very high between-study heterogeneity, underscoring a preclinical-to-clinical translational gap.
findings.claim_source_sentence: 11 studies were identified, and the risk of bias in most studies was unclear generally.
findings.evidence: SYRCLE-assessed systematic review and meta-analysis of 11 preclinical exosome studies for diabetic peripheral neuropathy; pooled effects large but heterogeneity I2 up to ~92%.
findings.effect_size_source_sentence: Pooled analyses demonstrated that exosome improved the nerve conduction velocity [MCV (SMD = 4.71 [2.18;7.25], P = 0.0003; I²= 91.8%), SCV (SMD = 1.07 [0.30;1.85], P = 0.0069; I²= 85.3%)], may restore IENFD [SMD = 1.46 [-0.85; 3.77], P = 0.2164; I²=88.7%], alleviated neuropathic pain [mechanical allodynia (SMD= -0.27 [-1.02;0.47], P = 0.4697; I = 85.0%), thermal hyperalgesia (SMD= -1.48 [-2.45;-0.50], P = 0.003; I = 88.4%)]
findings.study_system: preclinical diabetic peripheral neuropathy models (exosome therapy)

findings.claim: A systematic review of 78 preclinical spinal-cord-stimulation studies (SYRCLE-assessed, risk of bias unclear) concluded translatability between species is a lingering problem and issued recommendations to improve the reproducibility of the models.
findings.claim_source_sentence: Finally, we make recommendations for future research to improve the reproducibility of the described models and results and to progress the scientific foundation for this therapy.
findings.evidence: Full-text systematic review and post-hoc meta-analysis of 78 preclinical SCS studies; risk of bias assessed with SYRCLE and judged unclear.
findings.study_system: preclinical spinal cord stimulation models (mostly rats)

findings.claim: A systematic review of cannabinoids for ocular pain found only 4 of 479 screened records eligible, with methodological/design issues raising risk-of-bias concerns and too few studies for generalization or meta-analysis.
findings.claim_source_sentence: Methodological and design issues raise concern of risk of bias and the amount of studies is too small for generalization.
findings.evidence: PRISMA systematic review; 2471 records retrieved, 479 after de-duplication, only 4 eligible; meta-analysis impeded.
findings.effect_size: 4 of 479 records eligible
findings.effect_size_source_sentence: Eleven records result from title and abstract screening to meet the inclusion criteria; only 4 results are eligible for inclusion in the qualitative synthesis impeding meta-analysis.

findings.claim: In 11 pre-injury-exercise neuropathy studies, poor reporting meant risk of bias could not be estimated for most studies and planned sensitivity analyses were impossible, making clinical translation inappropriate despite a significant allodynia effect.
findings.claim_source_sentence: Thirdly, risk of bias analysis revealed poor reporting of essential details related to the design and conduct of the included experiments.
findings.evidence: Full-text SYRCLE-assessed systematic review and meta-analysis of 11 studies; five RoB domains all 'unclear' due to missing methodology; allodynia SMD -1.24.
findings.effect_size: mechanical allodynia SMD -1.24 (95%CI -1.87 to -0.61)
findings.effect_size_source_sentence: Mechanical allodynia scores, measured with von Frey filaments, were significantly better in the pre-injury exercise group compared to and non-exercise control (pooled data, 6 studies, 7 interventions, n=114, SMD -1.24, 95%CI: -1.87 to -0.61)

findings.claim: A meta-epidemiologic reanalysis of 15,635 animals showed experimental stroke studies that failed to blind ischemia induction or used healthy (non-comorbid) animals overstated intervention efficacy by roughly 12-13%.
findings.claim_source_sentence: Studies that included unblinded induction of ischemia reported effect sizes 13.1% (95% CI, 26.4% to 0.2%) greater than studies that included blinding, and studies that included healthy animals instead of animals with comorbidities overstated the effect size by 11.5% (95% CI, 21.2% to 1.8%).
findings.evidence: Meta-meta-analysis of 13 experimental-stroke meta-analyses (15,635 animals) quantifying the impact of design flaws on infarct-size effect estimates.
findings.effect_size: unblinded induction +13.1%; healthy animals +11.5%
findings.effect_size_source_sentence: Studies that included unblinded induction of ischemia reported effect sizes 13.1% (95% CI, 26.4% to 0.2%) greater than studies that included blinding, and studies that included healthy animals instead of animals with comorbidities overstated the effect size by 11.5% (95% CI, 21.2% to 1.8%).

findings.claim: A meta-analysis of 30 RhoA/ROCK spinal-cord-injury studies estimated 30% of experiments remained unpublished; correcting for this publication bias cut the apparent 21% locomotor benefit to 15%, and lower-quality studies reported larger effects.
findings.claim_source_sentence: Assessment of publication bias by the trim and fill method suggested that 30% of experiments remain unpublished.
findings.evidence: SR/MA of 30 studies (725 animals) with Egger regression and trim-and-fill; 9-item quality checklist; low quality associated with larger neurobehavioural estimates.
findings.effect_size: efficacy 21% (95% CI 16.0-26.6) falling to 15% after publication-bias adjustment (27% overestimate)
findings.effect_size_source_sentence: Inclusion of these theoretical missing studies suggested a 27% overestimation of efficacy, reducing the overall efficacy to a 15% improvement in locomotor recovery.

findings.claim: A meta-analysis of 549 spinal-cord-injury studies (9,535 animals) found more than half did not report blinded assessment, overstating effect size by 7.2%, with 2-41% of experiments estimated unpublished.
findings.claim_source_sentence: More than half of the studies (51.2%) did not report blinded assessment, constituting a likely source of evaluation bias, with an overstated effect size of 7.2%.
findings.evidence: Meta-regression of 549 preclinical SCI studies; neurobehavioural improvement 26.3%; publication-bias correction reduced effect by 0.9-14.3%.
findings.effect_size: 51.2% not blinded (+7.2% overstatement); 26.3% overall improvement
findings.effect_size_source_sentence: Overall, the included interventions reported a neurobehavioral outcome improvement of 26.3% (95% confidence interval 24.3-28.4).

findings.claim: In 11 Ginsenoside-Rg1 stroke studies (178 animals), no study reported a sample-size calculation and only 2 reported blinded outcome assessment; the entirely positive literature and Egger test indicated publication bias and probable effect-size overestimation.

conflicts.nature_of_conflict: Prescription for improving preclinical reliability: increasing statistical power/sample size within a single standardized laboratory (power view) versus the finding that larger single-lab samples worsen effect-size accuracy unless samples are heterogenized across laboratories.

papers.value_source_sentence: More than half of the studies (51.2%) did not report blinded assessment, constituting a likely source of evaluation bias, with an overstated effect size of 7.2%.
Inclusion of these theoretical missing studies suggested a 27% overestimation of efficacy, reducing the overall efficacy to a 15% improvement in locomotor recovery.

figure_data.what_it_reveals: Across independent preclinical meta-analyses in stroke and spinal cord injury, design flaws (no blinding, healthy animals) and publication bias each inflate reported efficacy by roughly 7-27%, a convergent quantification of how internal-validity failures distort the preclinical evidence base.

caveats: Metrics differ: two report percentage-point effect-size inflation from a single design item (blinding), one reports proportional efficacy overestimation from publication-bias correction.
Denominators are animals pooled across differing numbers of meta-analyses/studies.

mandatory_caption_caveats: Crossley (13.1%) and Watzlawick2019 (7.2%) are percentage-point effect-size inflations from different single design items (blinded induction of ischemia vs blinded outcome assessment).

Watzlawick2014's 27% is a proportional efficacy overestimation from publication-bias correction (21% to 15%), not a percentage-point figure. Models differ (stroke vs spinal cord injury; Watzlawick2014 is RhoA/ROCK-specific).
